articles.title: Global Market: Japanese investors extend foreign bond selling streak to four weeks
articles.content: Japanese investors sold foreign bonds for a fourth consecutive week, pushing year-to-date net outflows to 5.34 trillion yen, the highest since 2022. Rising domestic bond yields are encouraging capital repatriation, while foreign investors increase Japanese bond and equity holdings. However, life insurers’ limited selling suggests repatriation remains gradual.

articles.title: Indian Bank reports a Rs 1,388 crore gain from sale of NSE shares
articles.content: Indian Bank gained Rs 1,388 crore from the NSE listing, boosting second-quarter non-interest income by 50% to Rs 3,953 crore. Meanwhile, Canara Bank and UCO Bank reported declines in other income, reflecting weaker treasury earnings.

articles.title: Rupee relief comes with disruptions in financial markets
articles.content: The Reserve Bank of India took decisive steps to stabilize the rupee, significantly affecting financial markets. New constraints led to skyrocketing hedging costs and dwindled liquidity in the forex sector. Moreover, bond yields soared to their highest in three years due to escalating oil prices and foreign outflows. Banks brace for possible downturns and reduced foreign-exchange dealings in the next quarter.

articles.title: Rupee rises 20 paise to 94.79 against US dollar in early trade
articles.content: The rupee reached 94.79 against the US dollar following structural forex interventions by the Reserve Bank of India. Elevated crude oil prices and declining equity markets limited the currency's gains. The dollar index decreased by 0.54 per cent, reflecting the dollar's weakened strength. While US retail sales exceeded forecasts, the Producer Price Index was unexpectedly high. Foreign Institutional Investors also offloaded significant equities on Thursday, impacting domestic market performance.
